Using this information, calculate the great-circle distance between the primary container port serving the geographic region named on the box and the global headquarters of the developer of that bot protection system. Return the result in kilometers, rounded to the nearest integer.

**Image:** The cardboard box behind the two cats has "…NESQLAND" printed on it — i.e., **Queensland** (Australia). The primary container port serving Queensland is the **Port of Brisbane** (≈ 27.38°S, 153.18°E), Queensland's largest multi‑cargo/container port.

**Audio:** The narration describes **reCAPTCHA v3**, the bot‑protection system developed by **Google**, whose global headquarters is the **Googleplex, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California** (37.422°N, 122.084°W).

**Calculation:** Applying the haversine formula (Earth radius 6371 km) between (−27.3802, 153.1802) and (37.422, −122.084) yields ≈ 11,386.6 km. (Alternative precise port coordinates give 11,388–11,396 km, so the result is ~11,390 km regardless.)

<answer>11387</answer>

The great-circle distance between the Port of Brisbane (serving Queensland, as named on the box) and Google's headquarters (developer of reCAPTCHA v3, mentioned in the audio) is approximately **11,387 km** (~11,400 km).
